question:
Let G = (V, E) be a finite directed acyclic graph with |E| > 0. Which of the following must be true?
I. G has a vertex with no incoming edge.
II. G has a vertex with no outgoing edge.
III. G has an isolated vertex, that is, one with neither an incoming edge nor an outgoing edge.
options: I and III only
None of the above
I and II only
II and III only
I, II, and a vertex with one outgoing edge
I, II, and a vertex with one incoming edge
All of the above (I, II, III)
II only
I only
III only
model_outputs:
In a directed acyclic graph (DAG), there are no cycles, meaning that for any vertex, there is a unique path from any other vertex to it. 

I. G has a vertex with no incoming edge: This must be true. In a DAG, there must be at least one vertex with no incoming edges, as otherwise, there would be a cycle (if every vertex had an incoming edge, there would be a path from that vertex back to itself).

II. G has a vertex with no outgoing edge: This must also be true. Similar to the first point, in a DAG, there must be at least one vertex with no outgoing edges, as otherwise, there would be a cycle (if every vertex had an outgoing edge, there would be a path from that vertex back to itself).

III. G has an isolated vertex, that is, one with neither an incoming edge nor an outgoing edge: This is not necessarily true. An isolated vertex would mean that there is a vertex in the graph that is not connected to any other vertex, which is not a requirement for a DAG. 

Therefore, the correct answer is (C) I and II only.
